EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for lentils (pulse). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-SA-2022-0033 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 14 February 2022 and the current registration period extends to 13 February 2025. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Frances O'Brien is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2016. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description
The registered premises comprise the receival and storage complex at 88 Port Wakefield Road, Balaklava SA 5461. The area is approximately 35.1 ha. The boundary is the external fenceline of the farm.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.2 Services and Utilities
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: lentils is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of lentils. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

Hygiene and Sanitation Program (DDPE-HSP-001):
• Pre-season: full clean-down of receival pit, conveyors, pre-cleaner, gravity table, colour sorter and packing lines.
• During season: colour sorter air nozzles cleaned daily; packing tables sanitised between shifts.
• Personnel: handwash on entry; no food in processing area; dust masks and gloves provided.
• Records: Cleaning Register (DDPE-CLN-01) signed after each event.

Waste Management Procedure (DDPE-WMP-001):
• Pre-cleaner trash / weed seeds: collected in sealed bins; removed to composting weekly.
• Dust: cyclone collector emptied weekly; disposed to composting.
• Reject bags: damaged or misprinted bags recycled through approved contractor.
• Chemical waste: fumigant containers disposed per APVMA label; manifest maintained.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMESAED]
No formal pest control program is documented for Goulburn Murray Irrigation Co. No bait station map, monitoring schedule, contractor engagement or corrective action procedures are included.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMESAED]
No documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch for Goulburn Murray Irrigation Co. No lot coding, one-step-back/forward procedures, or recall protocol.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan.

Failed Goods Procedure (DDPE-FGP-001):
• Mycotoxin exceedance: lot placed on HOLD; re-test; if confirmed — downgrade to feed or destroy.
• Pesticide MRL failure: quarantine; reject export; notify grower; DAFF notified.
• Foreign material detection: stop line; remove contaminant; inspect batch; re-run.
• Non-conformance records maintained in DDPE-NCR register.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

Phytosanitary Security (DDPE-PSP-001):
• Export-cleared bags stored in sealed shed; access restricted.
• Fumigation certificate linked to dispatch docket.
• Container inspection before loading; seal number recorded.
• DAFF phytosanitary certificate issued per consignment.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Yorke Grain and Pulse is a registered export establishment located at 88 Port Wakefield Road, Balaklava SA 5461, SA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-SA-2022-0033 and is registered to handle and export Chickpeas under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Chickpeas.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

LED high-bay luminaires throughout: 550 lux processing, 440 lux storage, 418 lux load-out. All levels comply with AS/NZS 1680.2.1. Photocell-activated perimeter lighting for after-hours vehicle movements.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 2 toilets, 2 hand basins (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Internal surfaces: smooth-finish epoxy-sealed concrete floors with 80 mm coved skirting; smooth food-grade colourbond wall linings to 2.4 m; recessed drains with stainless-steel grates. All equipment on adjustable SS feet ≥150 mm off floor. Equipment housings open fully for pressure-wash access. Cleaning schedule specifies full washdown between commodity lots.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (3000 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1701 Rev 2): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

All areas are clean and tidy at inspection. Floors swept and dry — no accumulated chickpeas residue, spillage or debris observed. Wall surfaces free from dust and product residue. Equipment cleaned after each production run per cleaning schedule. Amenities block clean; consumables stocked. Drain covers in place and clear.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

No pest activity detected at most recent internal inspection. All rodent bait stations serviceable and baited — no evidence of feeding. Insect monitoring traps (pheromone and sticky) show no target species above threshold levels. No evidence of bird ingress. Last fumigation: 2024 (routine, bin rotation).

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMESA PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. ESTABLISHMESA INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Yorke Grain and Pulse used in horticultural packing and cold-chain export operations for Cucumbers. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Cucumbers during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay

After each produce intake: Remove all packing material (bins, cartons, netting) from dock. Sweep floor of organic debris (leaves, soil, rejected produce). Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Apply to floor with scrubbing brush, allow 3-minute contact time, then rinse with pressure hose ensuring all residue is cleared to drain. Check dock door seals for damage. Sign intake log on completion.
Grading & Sorting Line

After each production run: Power down and isolate grading line before cleaning. Remove produce residue from conveyor belts and rollers manually. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20. Apply to belt surfaces, brushes, and rollers. Contact time 5 minutes. Wipe down all surfaces and rinse with clean water. Inspect brushes for wear or product trapping. Restart test run to confirm mechanical function. Record in Grading Log.
Packing Area / Line

End of each shift: Clear all produce from packing tables and conveyor line. Remove used packaging film, cartons, and waste to the external waste bay. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe packing tables, scales, and conveyor surfaces. Sweep and mop floor. Check under conveyor for accumulation. Packing Supervisor signs shift cleaning record before end of shift.
Cold Storage / Coolrooms

Monthly and between commodity loads: Defrost evaporator coils per manufacturer instructions. Prepare AcidRinse 500 at 1:50. Apply to evaporator surfaces and drain tray to remove mineral scale. Rinse. Prepare QuatSan 100 at 1:100. Wipe all internal wall panels, shelving, and floor. Clear floor drains of accumulated organic material. Record temperature before re-loading. Cold Store Manager signs maintenance log.
Pre-Cool Chamber

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Pre-Cool Chamber in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMESA OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Areas prone to organic residue accumulation include floor drain channels, conveyor return runs, and spaces under grading machinery. These areas are cleaned daily or as required to prevent fermentation, mould growth, and pest attraction.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System
Paper-based cleaning records are maintained in a ring-binder located at the site office. Completed records are filed monthly and stored for at least two years.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES

ATP (adenosine triphosphate) swab testing is used monthly on critical food-contact surfaces to verify cleaning efficacy. Results are recorded in the Surface Hygiene Register alongside the cleaning log.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Where a cleaning deficiency is identified, the affected area is immediately re-cleaned before any product handling recommences. The deficiency, cause, and corrective action taken are recorded in the Non-Conformance Register. Repeat occurrences trigger a review of the relevant SOP.
11. ESTABLISHMESA CONDITION ASSESSMESA
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

At the most recent internal inspection (23 August 2025), all areas of Yorke Grain and Pulse were found to be in a clean and hygienic condition consistent with the requirements of this plan. No deficiencies were identified.
